title: When the Horizon Turns
premise: When a flood-swollen river in the borderlands of Vessany delivers a salvage chest stamped with the seal of Karstia—a nation erased from maps forty years ago—blacklisted mountain guide Freya Amberdale recognizes the crest from her missing father's letters. The chest points to a wrecked airship in the high glacial lakes, carrying proof of who betrayed Karstia and why her family name was buried with it. Racing a salvage fleet and the monsoon, Freya must cross terrain that got her banned from two countries, guided by a rival salvager who may be working both sides. At the wreck she learns her father helped sink the ship to hide the truth—and must choose between exposing it and protecting the descendants who built new lives on the lie. She surfaces the truth on her own terms, clearing her name but losing the mountain sanctuary she'd hoped to reclaim.
about_author: Mirabel Galloway is a former expedition cook who turned to writing after a decade of seasons in the northern ranges. She lives in a converted boathouse and claims she has never once been lost, only briefly unpublished.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Working an illegal guiding route along the Vessany border river, Freya watches floodwater cough up a bronze-stamped chest bearing the seal of dead Karstia—the same crest inked on her father's last letter. When border patrols close in, she takes the chest and runs. Beat: restless competence cracking into old grief.

chapters.title: The Seal of a Dead Nation
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Hiding in a river town, Freya opens the chest: a logbook fragment naming the airship Vesper Kestrel, sunk in the high lakes, and coordinates in her father's handwriting. A bounty notice with her face reminds her what capture means. Beat: the past stops being abstract and starts demanding payment.

chapters.title: A Guide Nobody Hires
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya seeks out Ivo Renk, the only outfitter who'll still sell her gear, and learns a corporate salvage fleet—Halvern Deep Recovery—has already chartered every boat north. Their target date: six tides before monsoon landfall. Beat: the race clock starts ticking; isolation sharpens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rival at the Dock
chapters.summary: Sefa Marun's POV. Sefa, Halvern's lead diver, is ordered to find whoever took the chest before the fleet sails. She clocks Freya at the dock but hesitates to report her, unsettled by the Karstian seal—her grandmother's nation too. Beat: two hunters recognize each other; loyalty begins to bend.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya bargains passage upriver with smuggler Osk by promising him first claim on anything non-Karstian aboard the wreck. Osk warns the high passes are watched since 'the Amberdale incident.' Flashback threads reveal the blacklist's origin. Beat: shame confronted; the climb begins.

chapters.title: The Pass That Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya crosses the Vergha Pass alone after Osk's boat is impounded, navigating by memory of routes she was banned for pioneering. A storm forces her into a cave where she finds decades-old climbing gear stamped Amberdale Expeditions. Beat: the wilderness as judge; her father's shadow grows larger.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Country
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa secretly copies Halvern's survey charts of the lake basin and mails them to a Karstian diaspora archive, then lies to her captain about progress. Her grandmother's lullaby keeps surfacing. Beat: divided heart; sabotage disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Lake Below the Ice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya reaches the glacial lake and finds the Vesper Kestrel's mast breaking the surface as the glacier retreats—exposed now for the first time in forty years, which explains the fleet's sudden interest. She scouts dive points as the first tide of six ebbs. Beat: awe braided with dread; the prize is real.

chapters.title: Two Divers, One Wreck
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sefa arrives ahead of the main fleet to plant survey beacons and finds Freya already diving. Instead of a fight, they surface together when Freya's line snags, and Sefa says nothing to her superiors. Beat: enemies become reluctant allies over shared breath and shared bloodline.

chapters.title: The Logbook's Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Inside the hull, Freya recovers the captain's safe: the full logbook, minus pages torn out in a hurry. The remaining entries describe cargo 'too true to float' and name an officer: A. Amberdale, her father, listed as crew—not passenger. Beat: identity shaken; inheritance curdles into question.

chapters.title: Tide Three Turns
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Halvern fleet arrives early, led by director Corvel Brase, who reveals he knows Sefa tipped the archive and offers her a choice: help him or watch Karstian history get patented and sold. Sefa stalls. Beat: pressure doubles; betrayal wears a professional smile.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weather buoys confirm the monsoon will make landfall in four tides, not six. Freya and Sefa must dive the deep hold before the lake turns lethal, but the torn pages are missing—until Freya realizes someone else reached the wreck years ago. Beat: time collapses; paranoia and partnership tighten together.

chapters.title: Amberdale Expeditions
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following equipment traces in the wreck, Freya finds her father's old camp above the lake, and a journal explaining he tore the pages: they named the officials who sold Karstia out, men whose grandchildren now run Vessany. He sank the truth to protect his family. Beat: the blacklist reframed—her father chose exile to keep her safe.

chapters.title: What Brase Wants
chapters.summary: Corvel Brase's POV. Brase captures Osk and learns Freya holds the journal. His plan isn't scholarship—it's leverage: the names could blackmail half the border governments, and he intends to sell them back. Beat: stakes clarified; this was never about treasure.

chapters.title: The Offer on the Ice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Brase corners Freya on the lake ice: her blacklists lifted, her father's name restored, in exchange for the pages. Sefa stands at his side, apparently turned. Freya asks for one night to decide. Beat: temptation made concrete; trust hangs by a rope.

chapters.title: Sefa's Tide
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reveals her defection was staged: she's copied the pages and hidden the originals in the diaspora archive's hands. But Brase anticipated her—the archive was raided at dawn. Only the copies in their heads remain. Beat: the plan frays; memory itself becomes the last vault.

chapters.title: Dive of the Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With Brase's divers sealing the wreck, Freya and Sefa make a final descent through the collapsing ice channel to recover the ship's bell—physical proof that can authenticate their testimony. Freya's air runs short; Sefa shares her regulator. Beat: climax of trust; the wilderness forgives nothing, but people can.

chapters.title: The Bell and the Storm
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The monsoon hits early. On the drowning shoreline, Brase demands the bell; Freya instead rings it on the ridge, signaling the diaspora villagers who arrive as witnesses, cameras running. Brase's fleet flees the storm rather than fight a crowd. Beat: public truth beats private leverage.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In the valley hall, the recovered names are read aloud from memory while elders verify them against songs and records no corporation could buy. Freya's father is named neither hero nor villain—just a man who chose badly for loving reasons. Beat: mourning without absolution; history re-homed.

chapters.title: The Price of the Truth
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Vessany lifts one blacklist but upholds the other; the mountains she loved remain closed to her. Brase escapes prosecution but loses his charter, his fleet, and his leverage. Freya realizes restoration isn't return. Beat: bittersweet accounting; inheritance accepted on its real terms.

chapters.title: Where the Horizon Turns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Sefa guide a small group of young Karstians to the lake to see the Vesper Kestrel's mast one last time before winter ice takes it. Freya leaves her father's journal with the community, keeping only one page—his apology to her. Beat: release; the horizon turns toward something unowned.

chapters.title: First Ascent, New Name
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Months later, Freya leads a legal expedition under a newly registered outfitting license—Amberdale & Marun—into ranges that never knew her disgrace, only her skill. A letter arrives from the second country: the last blacklist revoked. She folds it away unread until camp. Beat: earned homecoming; identity chosen, not inherited.
